answer: The cheapest real defence: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because spiral only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, ivory is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any whisper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
